title: Strategic sponsor QBR script and renewal notes
body:
Purpose:
This is a working draft: a concise script and follow-up sequence for executive sponsors ahead of and after quarterly business reviews (QBRs). Primary goal: keep sponsor-level stakeholders confident in strategic outcomes, reduce renewal risk, and align exec priorities with product roadmaps. Secondary goal: provide a reusable email cadence and a simple renewal tracker snapshot to hand off to account teams.

Audience:
- Executive sponsor (CPO/CTO/Head of ML)
- Customer success manager (CSM) and renewal lead

Pre-read to attach (send 4–7 days before QBR):
- One-pager: Top 3 wins since last QBR (1 page)
- Simple usage & health dashboard (1 slide): key KPIs for prod vs test, latency, error rate, call volume, token spend trend
- Open roadmap items that impact the customer (bulleted list)

30-minute sponsor QBR script (phone / video)
- 0:00–02:00 — Quick hello, confirm time and ask if anything urgent to add.
  Script: "Thanks for carving out time. I’ll keep this tight — three things to cover: what changed, what we recommend, and any support you need from you/your org. Anything you want to add up front?"

- 02:00–08:00 — State top-line outcomes since last QBR (metrics + business impact).
  Talking points:
    • Active endpoints growth: +X% (month-over-month) — cite concrete feature/use-case.
    • Latency and reliability summary: 99.9% uptime, p95 latency Y ms (note any anomalies)
    • Cost/unit trend: per-token cost change and actions taken (batching, quantization).

- 08:00–16:00 — Highlight two customer wins and one open risk.
  Wins: short bullet on how Redwood helped reduce latency/cost or improved consistency.
  Risk: e.g., predicted spike during upcoming campaign, potential SLO impact, or integration gaps.

- 16:00–25:00 — Recommended roadmap moves and asks for the exec sponsor.
  Examples of asks: prioritization for an internal ticket, dedicated engineering time for security review, access to product metrics, or approval for a pilot on Dedicated capacity.
  Script: "To lock in the next phase we recommend A + B this quarter. We’ll need either a technical liaison or a short executive sign-off to proceed. Which would you prefer?"

- 25:00–30:00 — Confirm next steps, responsibilities and timing.
  Close: summarize 2 decisions, who owns them, and date for follow-up.
  Script: "Recap — we’ll (1) run pilot X by mm/dd — owner Y, and (2) present cost/benefit after 30 days. I’ll send a one-email summary right after this call. Thanks for your time."

Notes on tone and style:
- Keep it outcome-first and concise. Execs care about business impact, not implementation detail.
- Use precise numbers (not vague adjectives) when available. If numbers are incomplete, label them as estimates.
- Avoid product roadmap dives; present only top-level asks and potential business outcomes.

Two follow-up email templates (send within 24 hours):

1) Short executive summary (best when the sponsor is time-constrained)
Subject: Quick QBR recap & two decisions (Redwood / <Customer>)
Hi <FirstName>,
Thanks again for today — very helpful. Quick recap:
- Outcome highlights: [1–2 bullets: e.g., 18% latency improvement on purchase path; tokens per session down 12%]
- Decisions & owners: [Decision A — Owner, due mm/dd]; [Decision B — Owner, due mm/dd]
Next: we’ll start pilot X on mm/dd and share a 2-slide progress note after 30 days. If you’d like a 10-minute sync before then, say the word.
Best,
<CSM name>

2) Longer briefing (for sponsor + extended exec team)
Subject: QBR deck + recommendations — Redwood x <Customer> (detailed)
Hi <FirstName> and team,
Appended: 1-page wins + 1-slide health dashboard + 1-slide recommended roadmap items. Highlights:
- Business impact: [short paragraph with metrics tied to revenue/latency/cost]
- Risks & mitigations: [bulleted list]
- Asks: 1) Approve pilot of Dedicated capacity for payment-flow (owner, cost estimate, expected impact) 2) Allocate a 2-day security review window (owner)
Action items we’ll track: [table-like lines — see renewal tracker snapshot below].
Thanks,
<CSM name> & <Renewal lead>

Renewal tracker snapshot (example lines you can paste into a sheet) — minimal columns so execs can scan quickly:
Columns: account, ARR, renewal_date, renewal_owner, risk_level, next_action, notes
Sample rows (comma-separated):
Acme Corp, 420000, 2026-09-30, Samir Joshi, medium, schedule exec review by 2026-07-15, pilot approval pending capacity estimate
Bluefin Payments, 185000, 2026-06-15, Evelyn Park, high, escalate to VP CS + propose 10% credits for pilot, security checklist incomplete
Nova Retail, 90000, 2026-04-20, Asha Rao, low, on track, standard renewal cadence

Checklist for the QBR one-pager and slide deck:
- One-line business impact (quantified)
- Three top-level metrics with +/- since last QBR
- One line for open technical deps that require sponsor help
- Two recommended next steps with owners and dates
- 1 supporting customer quote (if available)

Playbook snippets for common sponsor asks (short answers to prep):
Q: "What happens if we exceed token budget in a quarter?"
A: "We first look at routing and batching options we enable immediately; if still above threshold we propose a temporary cap on non-critical endpoints and present a cost mitigation plan within 3 business days."

Q: "If latency spikes during campaign, how will Redwood respond?"
A: "Automatic fallback to secondary region/model variant, on-call SRE notification within 5 minutes, and follow up RCA within 72 hours."

Hand-off notes for renewal specialist (copy into CRM after QBR):
- Confirmed decisions and owners from sponsor call.
- Upload one-pager and health slide to account page.
- Create renewal opportunity in CRM with linked pilot ticket (if applicable).
- Set next exec touch date 60–90 days before renewal_date.

Open items / things to iterate on in this doc:
- Create a short fillable template for the one-pager (1:1 mapping to the checklist above).
- Add an optional 5–7 minute demo script for sponsors who prefer product demos.
- Add standardized quant language for risk levels (low/medium/high) with definitions tied to ARR percentages.

Quick version history:
- v0.1 2025-11-18: initial draft (Asha)
- v0.2 2026-02-28: added follow-up templates and renewal snapshot (collaborators)

End of draft.
